question.problem: Find the surface area of the part of the plane $z=2y-x$ that is subject to the constraints ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 9$ and $x\le 0.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=2y-x,\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 9,\,x\le 0\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221663/assets/3c6c556ec90138fa1f0b599c6afed9d093e5c1b10f7751a5fbe55f0add617e1d.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y-x)=-1, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y-x)=2,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(-1)^{2}+(2)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+1+4}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{6}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region $D$ can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 3,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula for polar coordinates, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\sqrt{6}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}\sqrt{6}\,r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\sqrt{6}\,r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{6}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}\,\text{d}\theta {\int }_{0}^{3}r\,\text{d}r \\  & =\sqrt{6}\cdot [\theta ]_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}\cdot {[\frac{{r}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\cdot \pi \cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi \sqrt{6}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
